control: Both candidates forbid security-level new risk while that same close has broken=true. This necessary risk-consistency repair is explicit and isolated from the memory effect; the old price book and all original evidence stay unchanged.
memory: When enabled, the first new protective full-exit instruction remembers that securitys fresh signal close. Any decrease of the actual filled-account risk cap records each currently quoted securitys close, including unheld names; an unresolved older anchor can only ratchet higher, never be lowered by further warnings. Repeated unfilled exit retries do not reset the anchor or recovery clock. Ordinary weight-drift trimming is not a new risk event.
readmission: An anchored security needs three consecutive fresh closes at or above its event price and above EMA10 before any new units are requested; all parent entry predicates also remain. A quote recovery or cancelled order is not funded recovery. Clear an anchor only after observing an actual inventory increase with prior confirmed health and a currently healthy quote. Parent actual-liquidation readmission requirements and latched protective sells remain in force. New risk on previously unquoted securities follows the unchanged twenty-observation warm-up; no future price supplies an anchor.
clock: Signals and event anchors use only the supplied close or earlier history. An actual fill is visible at its session close. A new event resets affected confirmation counters. No date, stock, industry, outside-universe or forecast input is added.
tradeoff: Event memory may avoid repeated losing rebounds but may delay profitable bottom participation; this must be measured, not assumed. It is neither a permanent account-NAV recovery requirement nor an all-time-record-high entry rule.
